# pai setups

Orchestrator + worker combinations (save your own)

```
pai setups [command]
```

A setup says which model runs the main conversation and which provider the workers run on. "Last time" is how your latest session ran; the rest are built from your configured providers and anything you saved. Every enabled local provider (loopback, e.g. a model on this machine) gets "anthropic + <provider> workers": Anthropic orchestrates, the local model does the work, for that session only. The list reads your configuration and cooldowns; it does not contact any provider.

```sh
pai setups
pai setups save "my mix"
pai webseiten --with "anthropic + glm workers"
pai new ~/code/app --with "anthropic + flashnext-iq3 workers"
```

See also: `pai`, `pai providers`

### pai setups save

Save the current combination under a name

```
pai setups save NAME [options]
```

Saves how your most recent session ran (its orchestrator) together with the provider workers run on now. Name them explicitly with --orchestrator and --workers.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Name for the setup, e.g. "opus + glm" |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--orchestrator PROVIDER` | string | — | Provider that runs the main conversation (default: your latest session's) |
| `--workers PROVIDER` | string | — | Provider the worker classes run on (default: the active provider) |

```sh
pai setups save "my mix"
pai setups save "kimi + glm" --orchestrator kimi --workers glm
```

See also: `pai setups`

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pai setups save` | Save the current combination under a name |
